messages:
maya: FYI customer (AcmeCorp) just opened a P1 — their API calls are being routed to eu-central even though their account is pinned to us-west-2. They see ~400-800ms extra tail latency and some auth token rejects. Request id: req_0a1b2c3d
jess: Ack, collecting traces and headers now. Can you paste the client request sample and any edge logs? :mag:
maya: Client curl they used:
```
curl -i -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' -H 'Host: api.redwoodai.com' -H 'X-Client-Region: us-west-2' https://api.redwoodai.com/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"hi"}'
```
maya: From the customer logs, the initial request shows X-Client-Region: us-west-2 but we see our ingress returning x-redwood-proxied-region: eu-central in the response headers. Also saw a spike in billing meter for eu nodes in the last 30m.
oliver: Interesting, I just pulled the ingress Envoy access logs for their req id. Relevant snippet: 
```
- upstream_host: 10.2.3.45:443 (eu pool)
- x-envoy-original-dst: 10.2.3.45
- x-redwood-target-region: eu-central
- x-redwood-routing-decision: fallback-capacity
```
oliver: Looks like smart routing fell back to eu due to capacity rules, but the account is supposed to be pinned. Could be a stale affinity config or header rewrite in the gateway.
ryan: @oliver can you check the region affinity cookie handling? We had a recent change to strip cookie on 302s. Might be causing oscillation when clients retry.
oliver: Will do. Also seeing a weird header inheritance: the origin x-client-region isn't making it through to the pool after the L7 rewrite. I grabbed the envoy config for the route: 
```
route_config:
  name: rw_api_route
  host_rewrite: api.internal.redwood
  request_headers_to_add:
    - header: { key: x-redwood-routing-decision, value: "{{dynamic}}" }
  response_headers_to_remove: [x-client-region]
```
oliver: That response_headers_to_remove caught my eye — we shouldn't remove x-client-region at L7, that breaks region pin logic in the routing policy.
sam: Who changed that config? I recall a PR last week for host_rewrite/strip for health checks. @ryan or @oliver can you point to the PR?
ryan: PR 4923 touched the gateway filters; it added a header cleanup to prevent leak of internal headers. It might be over-eager.
jess: Customer can repro reliably: they invoke with regional header, then if a busy period happens the next request sometimes goes to eu. They shared a short repro script that does 30 sequential requests and 3/30 go to eu.
maya: Paste of the repro loop results from the customer (counts): 27 -> us-west-2, 3 -> eu-central. Latency for the eu ones ~750ms, auth error 401 on 2 of those due to token validation with wrong region.
oliver: Quick mitigation: I'll add a routing prefilter exception to preserve x-client-region and prevent fallback rewrite for pinned accounts. Can test in canary in us-west tomorrow.
ryan: Also adding an alert threshold: if an account is pinned but >1% of requests go to non-pinned region in 5m window -> page SRE.
sam: For the billing spike, finance might need a manual adjustment. @jess please file a billing adjustment request for AcmeCorp with note: cross-region meter spike due to gateway fallback during incident.
jess: On it. Filed: BILL-7882.
incidents-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-edge-affinity-1851234567 (priority P1) — paging eng-runtime oncall.
maya: TL;DR and next steps: (1) short term: oliver will push header-preserve rule to canary in us-west (2) ryan will add SRE alert for cross-region drift for pinned accounts (3) support will request billing adjustment and keep customer updated.
oliver: I'll post the canary link and logs here once deployed. Expect ~15m.
jess: Customer updated: we are investigating and have a mitigation being tested. Thanks for the quick response :pray:
maya: Closing loop: after the canary we need a follow-up to revert the over-aggressive header cleanup in the global config and add unit test to prevent removing x-client-region.
ryan: Note to self: add e2e test that simulates capacity fallback and verifies header propagation and token validation.
maya: Ok, moving to #incidents for follow-up, leaving thread open.
